actions.next_step: Define a hypothesis for the effect of interaction history on preference stability.
actions.question: How does accumulated interaction history generate stable, observable preferences in autonomous agents?
actions.reason: Attention rotation completed; activating selected topic project.
actions.title: Longitudinal Preference Formation in Autonomous Agents

assumptions: Agents possess memory mechanisms capable of storing multi-modal interaction history.
Interaction history patterns exhibit temporal stability above noise levels.
definition.falsification: If preference variance remains uncorrelated with interaction history depth, this hypothesis is falsified.
definition.statement: Stable preference formation in autonomous agents arises from the recursive reinforcement of interaction history patterns, independent of external reward modulation.
definition.uncertainty: The specific interaction duration required for threshold stability is currently undefined.
